meta.audience: The reader, and the Gentiles addressed from verse 23
meta.location: The land of Heth, and the house of Jared
meta.date: The reign of Omer; Moroni's warning written after AD 400
meta.unit: The oath of Akish and Moroni's warning (Ether 8)
principles: A plan proposed by reading an old record
An oath that binds by threatening the head
A warning addressed past the story to the reader

world_behind.title: Omer spent half his reign in captivity
world_behind.text: Verse 4 says Omer spent half his days in captivity. Ether 10:30 and 31 list five successive kings who spent all of theirs that way, so a Jaredite king in prison is the ordinary case in this book rather than the exception.

world_behind.title: The plan comes out of a book
world_behind.text: Verse 9 has the daughter of Jared point her father to the record their fathers brought across the great deep. Helaman 6:26 insists the opposite about the Nephite band, that their oaths did not come from the records at all; Ether 8:15 says these were the oaths given by them of old, handed down from Cain. The two books disagree about whether the plans were ever written down.

world_behind.title: Akish was the king's friend
world_behind.text: Verse 11 says Omer was a friend to Akish before the marriage was proposed.

world_behind.title: The oath is sworn on four things
world_behind.text: Verse 14 has them swear by the God of heaven, by the heavens, by the earth, and by their heads. Mormon 3:10 has the Nephites swear by the heavens and the throne of God to the same kind of purpose, so the record reports the identical form of oath at both ends of its history.

world_behind.title: Moroni traces the oaths to Cain
world_behind.text: Verse 15 says they had been handed down from him.

world_behind.title: Moroni withholds the wording
world_behind.text: Verse 20 keeps the text of the oaths off the plates.

world_behind.title: He says the same thing killed both nations
world_behind.text: Verse 21 says the combinations destroyed both this people and the people of Nephi. Moroni is writing after Mormon 6, so he can state as history what Helaman 2:13 could only predict about the second nation.

words.text: To praise a person in order to move him. Treated at Alma 20:4. The record uses the word five times and the King James Bible twice.
Skilled, practiced at something. Treated at Alma 10:31. It appears five times in the record and six in the King James Bible, usually of soldiers. Verse 8 applies it to the daughter of Jared.
Relatives by blood. Treated at Mormon 8:5. It appears three times in the record and twice in the King James Bible.
To let out what was meant to stay hidden. The record uses the word once, here, and never the King James Bible. It appears in the oath itself.
To strip by force. The record uses the word twelve times, none of them in the King James Bible, and lists it here among the purposes of the oaths.
To hold a thing up, or to keep it standing. The record uses the word twice and the King James Bible eight times. Verse 22 makes a nation's survival turn on it.
Led astray by deception. The record uses the word twice, here and at 2 Nephi 9:9, and the King James Bible five times, including Genesis 3:13.

phrases.term: Because of his cunning words, until he had gained the half of the kingdom
phrases.text: The method and the result in one clause. Verse 3 turns the half into the whole by force.

phrases.term: He had set his heart upon the kingdom and upon the glory of the world
phrases.text: Moroni's account of the sorrow in verse 7. The grief has a stated object.

phrases.term: Hath he not read the record which our fathers brought across the great deep?
phrases.text: The question that starts the plan. She points him at a book they already own.

phrases.term: I am fair, and I will dance before him
phrases.text: Her own part in the plan, offered first. The rest of the verse is the price she sets.

phrases.term: Will ye swear unto me that ye will be faithful unto me in the thing which I shall desire of you?
phrases.text: The oath asked before the deed is named. The order matters.

phrases.term: Whoso should divulge whatsoever thing Akish made known unto them, the same should lose his life
phrases.text: The penalty clause. Secrecy is enforced by the same threat as disloyalty.

phrases.term: The oaths which were given by them of old who also sought power
phrases.text: Moroni placing the oaths in a line. Verse 15 runs the line back to Cain.

phrases.term: For the Lord worketh not in secret combinations
phrases.text: The flat statement dividing the two. Verse 19 adds that bloodshed was forbidden from the beginning.

phrases.term: It hath been made known unto me that they are had among all people
phrases.text: Moroni's reason for withholding the wording. He says the thing is already everywhere.

phrases.term: Whatsoever nation shall uphold such secret combinations
phrases.text: The condition on the warning, sized to a whole nation.

phrases.term: Ye shall awake to a sense of your awful situation
phrases.text: What the Lord commands the reader to do. The command is to notice.

verses.label: v. 8–10
verses.title: A plan credited to a woman who is never named
verses.text: The record gives her a description, "the daughter of Jared being exceedingly expert," and then hands her the initiative twice over: she "thought to devise a plan," and verse 17 states again that "it was the daughter of Jared who put it into his heart to search up these things of old." Her speech runs to two full verses and contains the whole scheme, including the exact words her father is to use. Nothing in the chapter supplies her name. The record names Akish, Kimnor, Jared, Omer, Esrom, and Coriantumr in the same passage.

verses.label: v. 9
verses.title: A character citing a book the reader does not have
verses.text: The record has her argue from a document: "Hath he not read the record which our fathers brought across the great deep? Behold, is there not an account concerning them of old, that they by their secret plans did obtain kingdoms and great glory?" The record brought across the water is mentioned at Ether 1:3 and elsewhere as the source of the Jaredite history, and here it is used as a manual. The argument works only if the record is available to be consulted, which makes this the clearest statement in these books that the brought-over archive was still in use generations later.

verses.label: v. 15–19
verses.title: A practice given a genealogy back to Genesis
verses.text: The record does not treat the oaths as an invention. It traces them: "the oaths which were given by them of old who also sought power, which had been handed down even from Cain, who was a murderer from the beginning." The phrase matches John 8:44, "he was a murderer from the beginning," said of the devil rather than of Cain. Verse 19 then states the contrary principle in the record's own voice, "the Lord worketh not in secret combinations," and grounds it in a prohibition dated "from the beginning of man."

verses.label: v. 20
verses.title: A refusal to write, with the reason supplied
verses.text: The record marks the omission in the first person: "I, Moroni, do not write the manner of their oaths and combinations." The reason given is not danger but redundancy, "for it hath been made known unto me that they are had among all people, and they are had among the Lamanites." The same writer withholds material at Ether 13:13 and reports being forbidden at 3 Nephi 26:11, but here the decision is his own and the ground is that the reader already has access to the thing described.

verses.label: v. 23–26
verses.title: The chapter turns from the Jaredites to the reader
verses.text: The record breaks the frame with a vocative: "Wherefore, O ye Gentiles, it is wisdom in God that these things should be shown unto you." What follows is conditional and specific, that if such combinations "spread over the nation, behold, they shall be destroyed," with the warning repeated at verse 24 as a command to "awake to a sense of your awful situation." Verse 26 then states the purpose of the writing itself, "I, Moroni, am commanded to write these things that evil may be done away." A history of a vanished people is given an explicit present-tense use.

chapter.title: The plan begins with reading
chapter.text: Verse 9 has the daughter of Jared send her father to a record they already had. What she found there was a method.

chapter.title: The oath is sworn before the crime is named
chapter.text: Verse 13 asks for faithfulness in a thing not yet stated, and verse 14 supplies the penalties.

chapter.title: The penalty is the same for leaving and for telling
chapter.text: Verse 14 attaches loss of head and loss of life to both.

chapter.title: Moroni gives the oaths a lineage
chapter.text: Verse 15 runs them back to Cain, and verse 18 says the combination was formed even as they of old.

chapter.title: He refuses to record the wording
chapter.text: Verse 20 says the manner of the oaths stays out, since the thing is already among all people.

chapter.title: He names two dead nations in one line
chapter.text: Verse 21 puts the Jaredites and the Nephites down to the same cause.

chapter.title: The warning is aimed at a nation
chapter.text: Verse 22 sets the condition on whatsoever nation upholds such combinations.

chapter.title: The command is to wake up
chapter.text: Verse 24 asks the reader to see the situation for what it is once these things appear.

applications.title: Notice where a sorrow is anchored
applications.text: Jared's grief is explained by saying he had set his heart upon the kingdom and upon the glory of the world. Whatever you could not lose without collapsing is a fair description of where your heart is set.

applications.title: Watch what you read for
applications.text: She went to the record looking for a method and found one. The book was not the problem.

applications.title: Refuse an oath taken before the thing is named
applications.text: Akish asked for faithfulness in a thing he had not yet described.

applications.title: Notice who profits from your silence
applications.text: The penalty for telling matched the penalty for quitting.

applications.title: Trace who handed the idea to whom
applications.text: The verse follows the chain: the daughter put it into her father's heart, Jared put it into the heart of Akish, and Akish administered it to his kindred and friends. Ideas move through named people, and being able to say who handed you yours is worth something.

applications.title: Decline to publish the method
applications.text: Moroni says he does not write the manner of their oaths and combinations. Reporting that a thing exists and supplying working instructions for it are separate acts, and he draws the line on purpose.

applications.title: Wake up when you see it
applications.text: Recognizing where you stand is what the verse asks first.

applications.title: State what your work is for
applications.text: Moroni says he was commanded to write these things so that evil might be done away and people might be persuaded to do good continually. Writing the purpose down is how a hard project stays aimed at something.

questions.text: What have I set my heart on that would leave me sorrowful to lose?
What am I reading in order to justify something I already want?
What have I been willing to trade that was not mine?
Have I agreed to something before I knew what it was?
What am I keeping quiet that should be said?
What is common enough that I have stopped noticing it?
What situation am I in that I have not let myself see?
